full_judgment:
3. Respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 23 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Phulpur, Mymensingh for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession of the suit land. His case, in short, is that C.S. khatian No. 155 for .19 acre of land of the suit plot was published in the name of Ramgopal Moochi, who died leaving behind his son, Howlader Moochi and Howlader Moochi died leaving behind his son. Mohan Rabidas, who got the land by inheritance and he had been possessing the same. On 09.12.1999 Mohan Rabidas exchanged .10 acre of land including a rain-tree with .11 acre of land of the plaintiff by deed of exchange dated 09.12.1999 and delivered possession thereof. Since then the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land by erecting shop. The defendants had no right, title and possession over the suit land. The defendants wanted to purchase the suit land but the plaintiff purchased the suit land and as a result, the defendants were angry with the plaintiff. On 20.12.1999, the defendants jointly and forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and raised a few tin sheds and they had been residing there Defendant No. 1, Union Parishad Chairman, who created two deeds of sale from Arshad Ali and Moezuddin Sarkar, who had no title and possession over the suit land. After that defendant No. 1 constructed a Union Council Office on the northern side of the suit land measuring .09 acre of land and he was in possession illegally. The plaintiff was in possession of .01 acre of land where he erected a shop. On 25.02.2001, the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff from .01 acre of land. Hence the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit. 

 4. Defendant No.1 and 9 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the plaintiff has no cause of action. The suit is not maintainable and it is barred by limitation. It is also barred by the principles of estoppel, acquiescence, waiver and admission and the plaintiff is not entitled to get any relief. Their further case is that .19 acre of land of suit plot No. 476 was recorded in the name of Chandra Kishore Tarafder in the C.S. khatian as the kayemi mukarqami jote. Ram Gopal Moochi left the suit land. Chandra Kishore died leaving behind only son Mohindra Kishore who settled .14 acre of land to Anu Sarker and .05 acre of land to one Fayez Uddin of the suit plot. However, only .04 acre of land has been recorded in the name of Arshad Ali @ Ashraf Ali, the heir of Ann Sarker, erroneously in place of .14 acre of land in ROR Khatian No. 362. Accordingly, .05 acre of land has been recorded in the name of Fayez Uddin in ROR Khatian No. 361 and ROR tenants Ashraf Ali and Fayez Uddin transferred the entire .19 acre of land in favour of the then Chairman of the Union Council by two registered deeds of sale dated 28.07.1965 and 03.08.1965. Since then the Union Council has possessed the suit land. The defendants never dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
